I fixed the bug in the format-selector parser in `youtube_dl/YoutubeDL.py` (around line 958). The failing test now passes, along with the other 13 tests in `test/test_YoutubeDL.py`.

**The bug:** when the parser hit a `/` (for example `a/b`, meaning "use `a`, otherwise `b`"), it added the either-or selector straight to its result list and then cleared the current selector. So if a `,` came after it, as in `a/b,c`, the parser added that cleared value, `None`, to the list as well. Building the selector function then crashed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'type'`.
